title: Quality gates: dashboards + alert rules (pass rate, failure spikes, latency, flake rate)
author: Sergio Costa
description: Adds first-class observability for Optimize quality gate runs. This PR introduces (1) a Grafana dashboard for the full gate-run funnel (created → running → passed/failed/overridden), (2) Prometheus alert rules for gate failure spikes, flake rate regressions, and gate execution latency/SLO breaches, and (3) runbook links + consistent labels so we can slice by config_type (batching/cache/quant_profile), model_family, route_id, account_tier, and region. Motivation: we’re rolling out mandatory gating ahead of applying Optimize recommendations; we need to catch (a) real quality regressions, (b) eval-harness instability/flaky suites causing false blocks, and (c) infrastructure constraints causing timeouts (notably EU-West). Design notes: alerts avoid paging on single-run failures; they trigger on burn-rate / sustained increases and include a ‘possible flake’ annotation when rerun aggregation indicates high variance. Dashboard includes deep links back into Console (gate run id) and the gate failure runbook for oncall. This aligns metric names/tags with the quality-gates observability standard and uses the new gate_run_id trace correlation field emitted by the Optimize service. Rollout: rules are initially deployed in ‘warning’ severity for 1 week; paging thresholds are enabled after we confirm baseline noise levels in limited production rollout.

alerts: add gate failure spike + pass rate drop alert rules with burn-rate windows
alerts: add flake-rate regression rule (quarantine signal) and annotation text
alerts: add gate execution latency SLO rule + non-paging warning stage

implementation_details: Dashboard panels: Gate runs (count) by status; pass/fail/override rate over time; failures by config_type + model_family; failures by route_id (top-k); flake score distribution; eval runtime (p50/p95/p99) split by region; queue time vs execution time; cost-of-gates proxy (gpu_seconds) when available; canary correlation panel (gate outcomes vs rollout promotion halts). Alert rules: (1) quality_gates_failure_spike: triggers when failed_rate over 15m is >3x 7d baseline and absolute failed_count >= 10, severity=page after the rollout period; (2) quality_gates_pass_rate_drop: burn-rate style, compares 1h vs 24h for pass_rate by config_type; (3) quality_gates_flake_rate_regression: warns when flake_score_p95 > threshold for a prompt_set_id cohort (no paging; directs to quarantine workflow); (4) quality_gates_latency_slo_breach: warns on p95 gate_duration_seconds > 20m for 30m window and pages only when paired with timeout_count increase (prevents noisy pages during GPU scarcity). All alerts include annotations with runbook URL + suggested triage tags and a pre-filled Grafana explore link.
review_conversation: Allison Grant: The panels look good, but please align naming with the observability standard (gate_run_status vs status) and make sure all alerts include route_id/account_tier labels for enterprise drill-down. Also: can we avoid paging on flake spikes until quarantine workflow is live? Sergio Costa: Updated label keys to match standard (gate_status, config_type, model_family, account_tier, region) and added route_id/account_tier breakdown variables. Flake rule remains warning-only and now includes ‘quarantine_candidate=true’ annotation. Sean Gallagher: For paging rules, we need multi-window burn-rate, otherwise we’ll page on brief eval-harness blips. Also add a guard that avoids paging when total_runs is low (new routes). Sergio Costa: Added two-window condition (5m + 1h) for failure spike and min total_runs >= 50 over 1h for paging. Also added a rollout-phase toggle: severity=warning by default, can be flipped to page via values file. Caleb Johnson: Do we have trace correlation? I’d like the alert to link to traces by gate_run_id. Sergio Costa: Added annotation gate_run_id and query template for Tempo trace search; also included a panel that shows trace sample links for top failures. Connor O'Brien: Please ensure rules compile under our promtool CI and don’t exceed label cardinality limits (route_id can explode). Sergio Costa: Limited the rule group label sets to config_type/model_family/region/account_tier; route_id is dashboard-only with top-k queries. promtool passes.
ci_summary: Checks: lint (pass), jsonnetfmt (pass), grafana-dashboard-validate (pass), promtool (pass), unit (pass). One transient failure on grafana-dashboard-validate due to upstream schema fetch; rerun succeeded.
release_notes: Adds Quality Gates Overview dashboard and initial alert rules (warning-only by default) for gate failures, latency SLO breaches, and flake-rate regressions. Alerts include runbook links and are tuned to avoid paging on single-run failures.
